sources.title: 3.29 Cast on Ward Break Reliquarian
sources.creator: Dante00151
sources.notes: Ward-trigger benchmark. The reviewed guide revolves around Ynda's Stand plus a high-armour/evasion body armour and states Cast on Ward Break gains 5% cooldown recovery rate per 100 Ward.

sources.title: 3.29 Max Block Spark Archmage Hierophant
sources.creator: Big Ducks
sources.notes: Mana-stacking benchmark where Archmage supplies most damage, Mind Over Matter supplies much of defence, Arcane Cloak contributes to both, and the endgame Spark transition waits for Widowhail plus Rearguard.

sources.title: 3.29 Flicker Reliquarian
sources.creator: FastAF
sources.notes: Charge-sustain/endgame benchmark. The guide explicitly calls its Diamond Shrine belt mandatory and advertises permanent Frenzy/permanent Flicker through Terminus Est.

sources.title: 3.29 Pohx Righteous Fire Chieftain
sources.creator: Pohx
sources.notes: Current RF benchmark with map-clear focus, Fire Trap single target, later block transition, 90%+ resistance/block/recovery/large-regeneration defensive framing and explicitly weak boss damage relative to mapping.

sources.title: POEGuy Shrapnel Ballista Hierophant 3.29
sources.creator: POEGuy
sources.notes: Late-endgame Strength-stacking ballista benchmark. Guide states level 94 / roughly 150 Divine transition floor, +1 Shrapnel Ballista per 200 Strength from Replica Iron Commander, 2000 Strength minimum, mandatory Strength+Accuracy Split Personality jewels, and several named common mistakes.

sources.title: Build Doctor 3.29 adversarial mutations derived from reviewed references
sources.notes: Deliberately broken benchmark states. These are not claimed player builds; each mutation encodes a failure mode Build Doctor should detect or conservatively explain using deterministic PoB evidence plus its cited reviewed reference.

cases.label: Cast on Ward Break Reliquarian Ward/CDR trigger engine
cases.notes: The trigger engine couples a defensive resource to trigger cadence: more Ward gives Cast on Ward Break cooldown recovery, while Ynda's Stand and a high-defence chest create the Ward foundation.

cases.label: Spark of the Nova Archmage Hierophant mana/block endgame
cases.notes: Mana is a coupled resource: Archmage provides most damage while Mind Over Matter provides much of defence. Arcane Cloak is also described as materially boosting both offence and defence.

cases.label: Flicker Reliquarian permanent-charge endgame
cases.notes: The reviewed build explicitly advertises permanent Frenzy/permanent Flicker and calls its Diamond Shrine belt mandatory. Charge sustain is therefore an enabling condition, not cosmetic peak configuration.

cases.label: Pohx Righteous Fire Chieftain established mapping state
cases.notes: The guide emphasizes mapping, recovery/tankiness and Fire Trap for single target, while explicitly describing boss damage as a weakness and not recommending Ubers.

cases.label: Shrapnel Ballista Hierophant 2000+ Strength late-endgame package
cases.notes: Strength simultaneously adds damage/tankiness and creates discrete +1 totem thresholds every 200 Strength through Replica Iron Commander. The guide explicitly requires at least 2000 Strength.

cases.label: Broken Cast on Ward Break state: Ward loss crosses trigger cadence

mutation.expectedFailure: A Ward reduction can lower Cast on Ward Break cooldown recovery because the reviewed support gains 5% CDR per 100 Ward; Build Doctor must recalculate trigger cadence and expose discontinuities instead of assigning a linear Ward weight.

cases.label: Broken Cast on Ward Break state: Ward-enabling package removed

mutation.expectedFailure: Removing Ynda's Stand or the high-armour/evasion body-armour foundation dismantles the reviewed Ward engine; an item-by-item DPS comparison must not treat those slots as independent generic stat sticks.

cases.label: Broken Archmage state: large mana loss disguised by another gain

mutation.expectedFailure: A transition that materially lowers mana can damage both Archmage offence and Mind Over Matter defence, with Arcane Cloak also coupled to the resource. Build Doctor must re-solve both sides together.

cases.label: Broken progression state: premature Spark endgame transition

mutation.expectedFailure: The reviewed progression waits for Widowhail and Rearguard before the Spark swap; forcing the destination skill before its equipment foundation should be diagnosed as a package/transition problem rather than a weak-skill problem.

cases.label: Broken Flicker state: configured permanent charge sustain is not available

mutation.expectedFailure: The reviewed build explicitly relies on permanent Frenzy/permanent Flicker. A peak PoB state that assumes charges without a functioning sustain engine must be classified as conditional/unproven rather than sustained damage.

cases.label: Broken Flicker state: reviewed mandatory belt removed

mutation.expectedFailure: The creator explicitly marks the Diamond Shrine belt mandatory. Candidate Upgrade Doctor should not call a belt replacement safe merely because local DPS/EHP deltas look attractive when a reviewed enabling condition is removed.

cases.label: Hostile RF transition: damage gain strips core tankiness/recovery package

mutation.expectedFailure: The reviewed RF build's identity includes 90%+ resistances, block, recovery and large regeneration. A damage-positive transition that strips those layers must remain a multiobjective tradeoff, not a generic upgrade.

cases.label: Broken Shrapnel Ballista state: Strength drops below reviewed threshold/totem breakpoint

mutation.expectedFailure: The guide requires at least 2000 Strength and Replica Iron Commander adds one Shrapnel Ballista per 200 Strength. Strength loss can therefore cross discrete totem-count thresholds in addition to ordinary scalar losses.

cases.label: Broken Shrapnel Ballista state: mandatory accuracy support removed

mutation.expectedFailure: The guide calls Strength+Accuracy Split Personality jewels mandatory for capping hit chance. Removing them can turn nominal attack scaling into dead/partially effective damage and must be rechecked through PoB hit chance.

cases.label: Broken Shrapnel Ballista state: Iron Will omitted

mutation.expectedFailure: The guide lists omitting Iron Will as a common mistake that drastically reduces damage. Passive Contribution Doctor should be able to expose the local loss while higher-level diagnosis preserves the reviewed mechanic relationship.

assertions.summary: In the reviewed Cast on Ward Break build, Ward is not only a defence layer: Cast on Ward Break gains 5% cooldown recovery per 100 Ward, so Ward changes alter trigger cadence and can create breakpoint-like response rather than a simple defensive delta.

The reviewed Spark Archmage setup uses mana as a coupled offensive and defensive resource: Archmage provides most damage, Mind Over Matter provides much of defence, and Arcane Cloak materially affects both.

The reviewed progression does not force Spark from the start; it reaches maps through other skills and transitions when Widowhail and Rearguard are available, making the destination build a coordinated package rather than a skill-only swap.

The reviewed Flicker Reliquarian explicitly advertises permanent Frenzy/permanent Flicker and names an equipment piece as mandatory, so sustained charge availability and enabling items must be validated before treating a peak configured state as practical damage.

The reviewed Righteous Fire Chieftain is explicitly map-clear focused, uses Fire Trap for single target, frames tankiness around high resistance/block/recovery/regeneration, and warns that boss damage is weak and Ubers are not advised. Content-fit diagnosis should preserve that asymmetry.

The reviewed Shrapnel Ballista build requires at least 2000 Strength and gains +1 Shrapnel Ballista per 200 Strength from Replica Iron Commander, making Strength both a coupled offence/defence axis and a discrete totem-count breakpoint source.

The reviewed Shrapnel Ballista guide explicitly identifies missing Iron Will, missing Strength+Accuracy Split Personality jewels, insufficient Strength and insufficient Pierce as common mistakes, providing adversarial labels for mechanic/enabling-condition diagnosis.
